epochs.name: Taurus · the bull
epochs.oneLine: Jung places the bull before the ram in the changing archetypal dominants.
body: Jung names Taurus as the first of this sequence in his later Flying Saucers preface (CW10 ¶589), rather than assigning it fixed dates in Aion.

The atlas uses two equal 2,143-year months before year 0 to make the sequence traversable. These ancient boundaries are display approximations calculated from Aion ¶149 n.84, not dates Jung gives for Taurus.

passages.text: This transformation started in the historical era and left its traces first in the passing of the aeon of Taurus into that of Aries, and then of Aries into Pisces, whose beginning coincides with the rise of Christianity. We are now nearing that great change which may be expected when the spring-point enters Aquarius.
Starting from star "O" and assuming a Platonic month of 2,143 years, one would arrive at A.D. 2154 for the beginning of the Aquarian Age, and at A.D. 1997 if you start from star "a 113."

epochs.name: Aries · the ram
epochs.oneLine: Jung reads Christ as the last ram of Aries and the first fish of Pisces.
body: For Jung, the sacrificial lamb carries the departing ram symbolism into the new fish symbolism. The passage describes symbolic overlap, not a precise boundary.
The start at 2143 BCE is an equal-month display approximation. Jung does not fix this Aries boundary in Aion.

passages.text: But, to the extent that Christ was regarded as the new aeon, it would be clear to anyone acquainted with astrology that he was born as the first fish of the Pisces era, and was doomed to die as the last ram74 (άρνίον, lamb) of the declining Aries era.75

This transformation started in the historical era and left its traces first in the passing of the aeon of Taurus into that of Aries, and then of Aries into Pisces, whose beginning coincides with the rise of Christianity. We are now nearing that great change which may be expected when the spring-point enters Aquarius.
We said . . . that Isaac bore the form of Christ, but that the ram also seems no less to bear the form of Christ.
Who was that ram by the offering whereof was made a complete sacrifice in typical blood . . . who was prefigured thereby but Jesus . . . ?

epochs.name: Pisces · the two fishes
epochs.oneLine: Jung reads the Christian aeon through the tension of Christ and Antichrist.
body: Jung reads the two fishes as opposed principles within one aeon. His account of religious and psychic history remains an interpretation; Aion explicitly says no connection between Christ and the astrological age can be proved.
The atlas spans approximately 0–2200 CE. Jung qualifies the Aquarian boundary as indefinite, gives 1997 and 2154 for different reference stars, and also gives a 2000–2200 range.

passages.text: Although no connection of any kind can be proved between the figure of Christ and the inception of the astrological age of the fishes, the simultaneity of the fish symbolism of the Redeemer with the astrological symbol of the new aeon seems to me important enough to warrant the emphasis we place upon it.

Astrologically interpreted, the designation of Christ as one of the fishes identifies him with the first fish, the vertical one. Christ is followed by the Antichrist, at the end of time. The beginning of the enantiodromia would fall, logically, midway between the two fishes. We have seen that this is so.

Since the delimitation of the constellations is known to be somewhat arbitrary, this date is very indefinite. It refers to the actual constellation of fixed stars, not to fhe zodion noeton, i.e., the zodiac divided into sectors of 30° each. Astrologically the beginning of the next aeon, according to the starting-point you select, falls between A.D. 2000 and 2200.
Starting from star "O" and assuming a Platonic month of 2,143 years, one would arrive at A.D. 2154 for the beginning of the Aquarian Age, and at A.D. 1997 if you start from star "a 113."

epochs.name: The first fish · Christ
epochs.oneLine: Jung associates the first, vertical fish with the Christian light figure.
body: In Jung’s reading, Christ is the bright image of the self. Its exclusion of the dark side leaves a counterpart, the Antichrist.
The approximate year-1000 boundary follows Jung’s account of an enantiodromia, a reversal toward the opposite. It is a symbolic periodisation.

passages.text: Christ exemplifies the archetype of the self.5 He represents a totality of a divine or heavenly kind, a glorified man, a son of God sine macula peccati, unspotted by sin.

Astrologically interpreted, the designation of Christ as one of the fishes identifies him with the first fish, the vertical one. Christ is followed by the Antichrist, at the end of time. The beginning of the enantiodromia would fall, logically, midway between the two fishes. We have seen that this is so.

Thus God not only foresaw the enantiodromia that began in the year 1000, but also intended it. The Platonic month of the Fishes is to be ruled by two principles. The fishes in our text are parallel, like the oxen, and point to the same goal, although one is Christ and the other the Antichrist.

epochs.name: The second fish · Antichrist
epochs.oneLine: Jung traces the second fish from religious upheaval toward the modern crisis.
body: Jung connects the turn around 1000 with the Holy Ghost movement, religious dissent and later alchemy, Reformation and science. He does not treat each reformer as evil: Joachim may also carry a mediating spirit.
Jung’s description of rationalism and materialism as antichristian expresses his psychological reading of Western history, not the atlas’s judgement.

passages.text: Thus God not only foresaw the enantiodromia that began in the year 1000, but also intended it. The Platonic month of the Fishes is to be ruled by two principles. The fishes in our text are parallel, like the oxen, and point to the same goal, although one is Christ and the other the Antichrist.

If we see the traditional figure of Christ as a parallel to the psychic manifestation of the self, then the Antichrist would correspond to the shadow of the self, namely the dark half of the human totality, which ought not to be judged too optimistically.

The antichristian era is to blame that the spirit became non-spiritual and that the vitalizing archetype gradually degenerated into rationalism, intellectualism, and doctrinairism, all of which leads straight to the tragedy of modern times now hanging over our heads like a sword of Damocles,

With the year 1000 a new world begins, proclaiming its advent in a strange medley of religious movements such as the Bogomils, Cathari, Albigenses, Waldenses, Poor Men of Lyons, Brethren of the Free Spirit, Beguins, Beghards, etc., and in the Holy Ghost Movement of Joachim of Flora.

epochs.name: The commissure · the connecting band
epochs.oneLine: For Jung, the band between the fishes frames a passage through opposites.
body: Jung describes the commissure as the band of faint stars connecting the fishes and places the beginning of reversal midway between them.

The atlas uses approximately 1000–1500 for this transition, within the second-fish phase. Jung gives a rough sixteenth-century correspondence at the second fish’s tail; he does not date the band’s exact edges.

passages.text: The northerly, or easterly, fish, which the spring-point entered at about the beginning of our era,83 is joined to the southerly, or westerly, fish by the so-called commissure. This consists of a band of faint stars forming the middle sector of the constellation, and the spring-point gradually moved along its southern edge.

Astrologically interpreted, the designation of Christ as one of the fishes identifies him with the first fish, the vertical one. Christ is followed by the Antichrist, at the end of time. The beginning of the enantiodromia would fall, logically, midway between the two fishes. We have seen that this is so.

The point where the ecliptic intersects with the meridian at the tail of the second fish coincides roughly with the sixteenth century, the time of the Reformation, which as we know is so extraordinarily important for the history of Western symbols.

epochs.name: Aquarius · union of opposites
epochs.oneLine: Jung expects Aquarius to constellate the problem of uniting the opposites.
body: Jung anticipates an individual confrontation with good and evil rather than a solution supplied by politics or philosophy. This is his expectation, not a promised future.
The atlas starts this display span at the upper edge of Jung’s 2000–2200 range. Its end at 4343 is an illustrative 2,143-year month; Jung supplies no historical events or fixed endpoint for Aquarius.

passages.text: If, as seems probable, the aeon of the fishes is ruled by the archetypal motif of the hostile brothers, then the approach of the next Platonic month, namely Aquarius, will constellate the problem of the union of opposites.

Since the delimitation of the constellations is known to be somewhat arbitrary, this date is very indefinite. It refers to the actual constellation of fixed stars, not to fhe zodion noeton, i.e., the zodiac divided into sectors of 30° each. Astrologically the beginning of the next aeon, according to the starting-point you select, falls between A.D. 2000 and 2200.

This transformation started in the historical era and left its traces first in the passing of the aeon of Taurus into that of Aries, and then of Aries into Pisces, whose beginning coincides with the rise of Christianity. We are now nearing that great change which may be expected when the spring-point enters Aquarius.
It will then no longer be possible to write off evil as the mere privation of good; its real existence will have to be recognized.

events.name: The spring point crosses into the Fishes
events.oneLine: Jung’s two anchor dates for the ingress of the spring point into the Fishes.
body: The row is Jung’s own astronomical anchor (J): the meridians of the two reference stars give the ingress “about the beginning of our era.” The epoch boundary in this atlas stays at year 0 as a symbolic display choice.

passages.text: The meridian of the star "0" in the commissure passed through the springpoint in A.D. 11, and that of the star "a 113" in 146 B.C.

events.name: The fishes at Denderah
events.oneLine: Jung observes two fishes facing the same way before Christianity.
body: Jung cites the first-century-BCE zodiac at Hathor’s temple as a counterexample to an ancient opposition of the fishes. The year is the atlas’s century midpoint.

passages.text: The zodiac from the temple of Hathor at Denderah (ist cent. B.C.) shows the fishes, but they both face the same way.

events.name: Jupiter–Saturn in Pisces
events.oneLine: Jung reads beneficent Jupiter and Saturn in conjunction as united opposites.
body: Jung reports three conjunctions in Pisces in 7 BCE and dates their closest approach to May 29. Its astrological sign is Pisces; the event lies before the atlas’s approximate historical year-0 boundary. No birthplace or earthly observing site is asserted.

passages.text: In the year 7 B.C. this famed conjunction took place no less than three times in the sign of the Fishes. The greatest approximation occurred on May 29 of that year, the planets being only 0.21 degrees apart, less than half the width of the full moon.37

events.name: Christ as the first fish
events.yearDisplay: Beginning of the Christian era · symbolic boundary
events.oneLine: Jung reads Christ as the first fish and the last sacrificial ram.
body: Year 0 is an atlas boundary for the beginning of the era, not a claimed historical birth year. Jung’s argument concerns the Christ image and the overlapping ram and fish symbols.

passages.text: But, to the extent that Christ was regarded as the new aeon, it would be clear to anyone acquainted with astrology that he was born as the first fish of the Pisces era, and was doomed to die as the last ram74 (άρνίον, lamb) of the declining Aries era.75

Astrologically interpreted, the designation of Christ as one of the fishes identifies him with the first fish, the vertical one. Christ is followed by the Antichrist, at the end of time. The beginning of the enantiodromia would fall, logically, midway between the two fishes. We have seen that this is so.
Christ exemplifies the archetype of the self.5 He represents a totality of a divine or heavenly kind, a glorified man, a son of God sine macula peccati, unspotted by sin.

events.name: Fishers of men
events.oneLine: The apostles as fishers: the age’s first symbolic catch.
body: Jung reads the gospel fishers (J) as the new age announcing itself in the symbol of its sign.

passages.text: There Christ wants to make Peter and Andrew "fishers of men," and the miraculous draught of fishes (Luke 5 : 10) is used by Christ himself as a paradigm for Peter's missionary activity.

events.name: The warlike lamb of the Apocalypse
events.oneLine: The Aries residue returns as the warlike lamb, Christ’s shadow-figure.
body: The ram of the declining Aries era comes back as the Apocalypse’s warlike lamb (J) — the age’s first shadow-figure, “umbra Jesu” in Jung’s reading of the counter-image.

passages.text: For although the monstrous, warlike lamb is a shadowfigure in the sense that he is the counterpart of the lamb who was sacrificed, he is not nearly so irreconcilable with Christ as the Antichrist would have to be.

events.name: Christ casts off his shadow
events.oneLine: Jung reads the Gnostic discarded shadow as a precursor of Antichrist.
body: Jung cites the Gnostic teaching of Christ casting off his shadow. The approximate year and tentative Rome placement come from the existing field occurrence, not a date assigned to the teaching by Aion.

passages.text: For instance, one of the things they taught was that Christ "cast off his shadow from himself." 23

If we see the traditional figure of Christ as a parallel to the psychic manifestation of the self, then the Antichrist would correspond to the shadow of the self, namely the dark half of the human totality, which ought not to be judged too optimistically.

events.place: Rome? (Valentinus; reported by Irenaeus, Adv. haer. I, 11, 1; II, 5, 1)

events.name: The vertical and horizontal fishes
events.yearDisplay: ~2nd century CE copy · existing field dating
events.oneLine: Jung uses the Farnese globe to distinguish orientation from moral opposition.
body: Jung describes a vertical northern fish and a horizontal southern fish. The existing field dates the Roman copy approximately; Naples is its later museum location, not a claim about the place of manufacture.

passages.text: This is the globe of the heavens from the Farnese Atlas in Naples. The first fish, depicted north of the equator, is vertical, with its head pointing to the celestial Pole; the second fish, south of the equator, is horizontal, with its head pointing West. The picture follows the astronomical configuration and is therefore naturalistic.76

events.name: The early Christian fish
events.oneLine: Jung locates the Christian fish symbol around 200 CE in Alexandria.
body: Jung follows Doelger in giving Alexandria around 200 as the first appearance of the Christian fish symbol. This reported chronology differs from dating the earlier fish motif itself.

passages.text: According to Doelger, the Christian fish symbol first appeared in Alexandria around A.D. 200; 71 similarly, the baptismal bath was described as a piscina (fish-pond) quite early.

events.name: The great, pure fish of Abercius
events.oneLine: Jung questions a purely Christian reading of the Abercius fish.
body: Jung dates the inscription after 216 and warns that its Christian origin is doubtful. The atlas uses 217 as a lower-bound display marker, not a precise composition date.

passages.text: Though the Abercius inscription, which dates from the beginning of the 3rd cent, (after A.D. 216), is of importance in this connection, it is of doubtful Christian origin.

events.name: The Pectorios inscription
events.oneLine: Believers as the “divine descendants of the heavenly fish.”
body: The eucharistic fish-meal inscription of Autun (J), a dating-uncertain pillar of the Christian fish record.

passages.text: In the Pectorios inscription (beginning of the fourth century), believers are called the "divine descendants of the heavenly fish."

events.name: Augustine’s king and priest
events.oneLine: Jung follows Augustine’s two fishes as ruling powers united in Christ.
body: Jung uses Augustine’s kingly and priestly interpretation to explain fishes as ruling powers. The approximate date comes from the linked field, not the quoted paragraph.

passages.text: To this end I must recall to the reader St. Augustine's interpretation of the two fishes in the miraculous feeding of the five thousand: for him they represent the kingly and the priestly person or power,91 because, like fishes surviving the tempests of the sea, they outlast the turbulence of the multitude. These two powers are united in Christ: he is the king and priest.92

events.name: Benedict and the latent age of spirit
events.yearDisplay: A few years after 529 · approximate marker
events.oneLine: Jung reports Joachim’s third age as secretly beginning with Benedict.
body: Jung says Joachim placed the beginning of the Holy Ghost’s third aeon with Benedict and a monastery built a few years after 529. Year 530 is approximate; the event presents Joachim’s chronology as Jung reports it.

passages.text: This third aeon, he says, had already begun with St. Benedict, the founder of the Benedictine Order (the first monastery was supposed to have been built a few years after 529).

events.place: Monte Cassino · monastery named in Aion ¶139

events.name: The war of the fishes
events.oneLine: The tanninim war: the age’s eschatological double, read by Rashi as fishes.
body: Jung calls the Talmud’s war of the tanninim (J) “probably the oldest testimony to the antithetical nature of the fishes”; Rashi’s gloss makes them two fishes at war before the Messiah.

passages.text: There will follow the war of the tanninim [sea-monsters], the war of Gog and Magog

The Talmud commentator Solomon ben Isaac, alias Rashi (1039-1105), remarks that the tanninim are fishes, presumably basing himself on an older source, since he does not give this as his own opinion, as he usually does.

events.name: Morienus and the inner work
events.oneLine: Jung traces alchemical self-knowledge back to Morienus.
body: Jung dates Morienus Romanus to the seventh–eighth century and reads the vessel’s maxim as a moral demand. Year 700 is a display midpoint; the linked occurrence supplies the geographical tradition.

passages.text: The idea itself is much older and goes back to Morienus Romanus (7th-8th cent.), in the saying which he wrote on the rim of the Hermetic vessel: "All those who have all things with them have no need of outside aid." 48

events.name: The reversal around 1000
events.oneLine: Jung places the beginning of the enantiodromia around the year 1000.
body: Jung interprets the second millennium as a reversal within the Christian aeon. His two principles still belong to one process; this is not a claim that every subsequent movement is evil.

passages.text: Thus God not only foresaw the enantiodromia that began in the year 1000, but also intended it. The Platonic month of the Fishes is to be ruled by two principles. The fishes in our text are parallel, like the oxen, and point to the same goal, although one is Christ and the other the Antichrist.

events.name: The Messiah expected in the Fishes
events.oneLine: The great conjunction in Pisces read as the Messiah’s clock.
body: From the 11th-century astrologers to Abarbanel (J, as Jung cites them), the Jupiter–Saturn conjunction in Pisces carries the messianic expectation — the age’s own astrology turned toward its sign.

passages.text: Jeremias8 adopts the same view and mentions that a Jewish commentary on Daniel, written in the fourteenth century, expected the coming of the Messiah in the sign of the Fishes.
This commentary is mentioned by Muenter in a later publication 9 as stemming from Don Isaac Abarbanel, who was born in Lisbon in 1437 and died in Venice in 1508.

events.name: The Cathar–Bogomil two fishes
events.oneLine: Jung conjectures Christ and Satanael behind the two fishes yoked together.
body: Jung traces the text to Basilius’s confession before Alexius Comnenus in 1111. Its place on the globe is the later Carcassonne archive named by Jung and carried by the existing field, not the place of that confession.
Jung calls the two-person interpretation a conjecture. The atlas preserves that qualification.

passages.text: Since the text is indubitably heretical and a Bogomil document at that, there can be no question of a uniform interpretation of the two fishes as Christ. It may be that they symbolize, as might easily be conjectured, two different persons or powers, from before the creation of the world: Satanael the elder son of God, and Christ the younger.

Our document is nothing but a Latin version of the report in the Panoplia of Euthymios Zigabenos, which in its turn goes back to the confession of faith made before the emperor Alexius Comnenus by the Bogomil bishop Basilius in the year 111 i.BB

events.name: The second fish surfaces
events.oneLine: Heresies, Joachim and the mendicants: the antichristian fish appears.
body: Jung dates the second fish’s surfacing (J) from the early-eleventh-century movements onward, and reads the era’s religious revolutions as its rising.

passages.text: It was therefore very natural, in an age which coincided with the beginning of the second Fish
These movements are also associated with the rise of alchemy, Protestantism, the Enlightenment, and natural science

events.name: Joachim’s third aeon
events.oneLine: Jung reads Joachim’s new age of spirit as potentially mediating the opposites.
body: Jung reports Joachim’s expected age of the Holy Ghost and his death in 1202. He distinguishes Joachim’s experience from the inflated claims of some adherents. The marker uses the linked field’s approximate dating.

passages.text: One of the most powerful and influential voices to announce the coming of a "new age of the spirit" was Joachim of Flora (d. 1202), whose teachings were condemned by the Fourth Lateran Council in 1215. He expected the opening of the seventh seal in the fairly near future, the advent of the "everlasting gospel" and the reign of the "intellectus spiritualis," the age of the Holy Ghost.

events.name: Latin alchemy emerges
events.oneLine: Jung connects Latin alchemy with the religious currents of the Middle Ages.
body: Jung places the beginnings of Latin alchemy around the twelfth and thirteenth centuries. Year 1200 is a display midpoint; the text does not assign this collective process one city.

passages.text: At about the time of the twelfth and thirteenth centuries we find also the beginnings of Latin alchemy, whose philosophical and spiritual content I have tried to elucidate in my book Psychology and Alchemy.

events.name: The Grail-stone as lapis exilis
events.oneLine: The fish-age’s compensating symbol of wholeness: the Grail as lapis.
body: Jung’s footnote chain (J) ties Wolfram’s lapsit exillis to the lapis exilis of the alchemists — the age’s counter-symbol of the self, parallel to Christ. Standard Grail philology (S) still debates the phrase’s origin; the reading here is Jung’s.

passages.text: Wolfram von Eschenbach calls the stone of the grail “lapsit exillis.” Arnold of Villanova (d. ? 1312) calls the lapis “lapis exilis,” the uncomely stone (Rosarium, Art. aurif., II, p. 210), which may be of importance for the interpretation of Wolfram’s term.

events.name: Joachim condemned at Lateran
events.oneLine: Jung marks the Church’s condemnation of Joachim’s teachings in 1215.
body: Jung places the condemnation inside a spiritually unstable epoch. The same paragraph also reports Joachim’s expectation of a new age; the atlas does not equate ecclesiastical condemnation with Jung’s own verdict.

passages.text: One of the most powerful and influential voices to announce the coming of a "new age of the spirit" was Joachim of Flora (d. 1202), whose teachings were condemned by the Fourth Lateran Council in 1215. He expected the opening of the seventh seal in the fairly near future, the advent of the "everlasting gospel" and the reign of the "intellectus spiritualis," the age of the Holy Ghost.

events.name: The everlasting gospel in Paris
events.oneLine: Jung follows Gerard’s claim that Joachim’s writings were the everlasting gospel.
body: Jung dates Gerard of Borgo San Donnino’s Introductorius to 1254 in Paris. It announces 1260 as the expected replacement of Christ’s gospel; that subsequent date is a prophecy, not an accomplished historical event.

passages.text: One of Joachim's followers, the Franciscan friar Gerard of Borgo San Donnino, proclaimed in his Introductorius in evangelium aeternum, which appeared in 1254 in Paris, that Joachim's three main treatises were in fact the everlasting gospel, and that in the year 1260 this would replace the

events.name: Pierre d’Ailly’s calculation
events.oneLine: Jung follows d’Ailly’s astrological conjecture about religious change.
body: Jung relates d’Ailly’s calculation of 1789 and its possible Antichrist interpretation. The year 1414 is the existing field’s dating of the text, not the date of the predicted event. Jung says he cannot claim to have understood every step of the argument.

passages.text: There are historical determinants that may have moved Nostradamus to give the year 1792 as the beginning of the new aeon. For instance, Cardinal Pierre d'Ailly, basing himself on Albumasar, writes in his Concordantia 5 on the eighth coniunctio maxima {u ό >? in τ), which had been calculated for 1693:

events.name: Abarbanel’s House of the Fishes
events.oneLine: The House of the Fishes as the house of justice and splendour.
body: Abarbanel’s commentary (J, as Jung cites it) expects the Messiah under the conjunction in Pisces.

passages.text: It is explained here that the House of the Fishes (K) is the house of justice and of brilliant splendour

events.name: The Renaissance turns outward
events.oneLine: Jung reads the Renaissance as a turn toward the second fish and modernity.
body: Jung connects the Renaissance with the spirit that culminates in the modern age. Year 1500 is a rough display marker for that process, not a beginning he fixes.

passages.text: The time of the Renaissance begins in the immediate vicinity of the second fish, and with it comes that spirit which culminates in the modern age.85

events.name: The Reformation threshold
events.oneLine: Jung places the Reformation at the passage toward the second fish.
body: Jung gives a rough sixteenth-century correspondence between the second fish’s tail and the Reformation. The atlas uses 1550 as a century midpoint; it does not invent a precise date or city from this collective process.

passages.text: The point where the ecliptic intersects with the meridian at the tail of the second fish coincides roughly with the sixteenth century, the time of the Reformation, which as we know is so extraordinarily important for the history of Western symbols.

events.name: Nostradamus writes to Henry II
events.oneLine: Jung reads the letter’s 1792 prophecy within the Christian aeon’s reversal.
body: Jung explicitly cites the 1558 letter, not merely the 1555 publication of the Centuries. Its predicted second Antichrist is part of Jung’s interpretation of the document. The existing field places the letter regionally in France.

passages.text: With this background in mind, I would like to mention the astrological prophecies of Nostradamus, written in a letter1 to Henry II of France, on June 27, 1558.

events.place: France (letter of June 27, 1558, to Henry II)

events.name: Dorn’s living stone
events.yearDisplay: Second half of the 16th century · existing field dating
events.oneLine: Jung reads the union in the stone as the adept’s own individuation.
body: Jung interprets the alchemical stone as a projection of the unified self, while preserving its transcendent character. The approximate year and regional location come from the existing field.

passages.text: The union of opposites in the stone is possible only when the adept has become One himself. The unity of the stone is the equivalent of individuation, by which man is made one; we would say that the stone is a projection of the unified self.

events.name: Lambspringk’s reversed fishes
events.oneLine: Jung reads Lambspringk’s fishes as a revitalized archetype of inner opposition.
body: Jung places the symbol near the end of the sixteenth century. The linked occurrence dates a later 1678 print in Frankfurt; that later print location is shown on the globe, not an asserted place of the original image.
Jung says he has found no text proving transmission of the Cathar fish into alchemy. The thread marks a comparison, not an established genealogy.

passages.text: I have not, however, come across any texts which would prove that the Catharist fish symbol was assimilated into the alchemical tradition and so could be held responsible for Lambspringk's fish symbol, signifying the arcane substance and its inner antinomy. Lambspringk's symbol appeared not much earlier than the end of the sixteenth century and represented a revitalization of the archetype.

events.name: Alchemy gives birth to science
events.oneLine: For Jung, alchemy gives birth to the age of science and then disappears.
body: Jung describes Mater Alchimia as a whole epoch beginning roughly with Christianity and giving birth to science in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Year 1600 is a display midpoint.

passages.text: "Mater Alchimia" could serve as the name of a whole epoch. Beginning, roughly, with Christianity, it gave birth in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries to the age of science, only to perish, unrecognized and misunderstood, and sink from sight in the stream of the centuries as an age that had been outlived.

events.name: The tail of the horizontal fish
events.oneLine: The Enlightenment as the chthonic fish’s tail: Christianity overthrown.
body: Jung’s seminar dating (J) of the second fish’s chthonic ascent, from the Goddess of Reason onward.

passages.text: And we entered the tail of the horizontal fish in about 1720, when the French Enlightenment began, when Christianity was overthrown and the Goddess of Reason was enthroned in Paris instead.

events.name: Faith and knowledge separate
events.oneLine: Jung diagnoses a rift in which faith lacks experience and science loses the soul.
body: Jung dates this rift to the eighteenth century. The atlas’s midpoint is approximate and the diagnosis is explicitly his.

passages.text: Thus, in the course of the eighteenth century, there arose that notorious rift between faith and knowledge. Faith lacked experience and science missed out the soul.

events.name: The revolutionary calendar
events.oneLine: Jung reads the French revolutionary calendar as a manifest antichristian turn.
body: Jung connects the calendar beginning on 22 September 1792 with Nostradamus’s renovation of the age. This is his reading of the French Revolution, not the atlas’s political judgement.

passages.text: The "renovation of the age" might mean a new aeon, and it coincides in a remarkable way with the new system of dating, the revolutionary calendar, which began with September 22, 1792, and had a distinctly antichristian character.®

events.name: The aeon running to its end
events.oneLine: The aeon “of the Fishes, now running to its end” — Jung’s 1951 summary.
body: Jung’s 1951 summary (J) of his own lifetime: the Antichrist figure anticipated and reflected in the wars. The arc’s shadow-counterpart is followed event by event in the atlas’s Turn reading.

passages.text: This unavoidable consequence is anticipated in the figure of the Antichrist and is reflected in the course of contemporary events, whose nature is in accord with the Christian aeon of the Fishes, now running to its end.

events.name: The aeon clock stated
events.oneLine: The two-fishes scheme taught: upright Christ-fish, horizontal chthonic fish.
body: Jung lays out the full precessional clock in seminar (J) — and adds “of course there are no definite lines in the sky which would indicate the exact borderline,” his own refusal of precision (see the Aquarius Horizon reading).

passages.text: According to the actual position of the astronomical constellation of the Fishes, one fish is upright and the other fish is horizontal, and between is the commissura, a sort of string from tail to tail.
Of course there are no definite lines in the sky which would indicate the exact borderline but in 1940 I 1950 we shall be in the vicinity of Aquarius.

events.name: The fish taught as the age-symbol
events.oneLine: The fish as Christ “after the constellation of Pisces” — the doctrine taught.
body: The aeon doctrine as seminar instruction (J), four years before the lectures that became Aion.

passages.text: The fish is Christ, so called after the constellation of Pisces, in which the vernal equinox entered after the beginning of Christianity.

events.name: The aftermath of the Second World War
events.yearDisplay: After the Second World War · 1945 display marker
events.oneLine: Jung reads the world’s division through the unrecognized inner opposite.
body: Jung compares the destruction left by the Second World War with the New Testament’s Antichrist expectations and describes the modern world’s division through an unconscious inner opposite. These are his psychological interpretations.

The atlas uses 1945 to place the war’s aftermath. This conventional historical display year is a site gloss; the quotation does not give an exact date. Aion’s 1950 writing date belongs to the source, not this event’s historical clock.

passages.text: The dechristianization of our world, the Luciferian development of science and technology, and the frightful material and moral destruction left behind by the second World War have been compared more than once with the eschatological events foretold in the New Testament.

Today humanity, as never before, is split into two apparently irrec- CHRIST, A SYMBOL OF THE SELF oncilable halves. The psychological rule says that when an inner situation is not made conscious, it happens outside, as fate. That is to say, when the individual remains undivided and does not become conscious of his inner opposite, the world must perforce act out the conflict and be torn into opposing halves.

events.name: Jung’s April fish
events.oneLine: The age-symbol surfaces synchronistically in Jung’s own life.
body: The famous synchronistic cluster (J): the piscis inscription, a patient’s fish pictures, fish-run embroidery — “Est homo totus medius piscis ab imo,” the century’s turn marked in his own material.

passages.text: That same morning I made a note of an inscription which read: "Est homo totus medius piscis ab imo." In the afternoon a former patient of mine, whom I had not seen for months, showed me some extremely impressive pictures of fish which she had painted in the meantime.

events.name: The Assumption declared
events.oneLine: The feminine counter-move as the age closes: symbols developing “through the ages.”
body: Jung reads the 1950 dogma (J) as the age’s closing counter-move — the example he gives of symbols developing through the ages, and the hinge the Turn reading’s compensation phase stands on.

passages.text: The solemn proclamation of the Assumptio Mariae which we have experienced in our own day is an example of the way symbols develop through the ages.

events.name: Aion published
events.oneLine: The aeon doctrine’s monument: Christian, Gnostic and alchemical symbols of the self.
body: The reading this atlas layer is built on (J), announced in its own foreword.

passages.text: My investigation seeks, with the help of Christian, Gnostic, and alchemical symbols of the self, to throw light on the change of psychic situation within the "Christian aeon."

events.name: Flying Saucers: a living myth
events.oneLine: The ufo round mandala “in the skies”: the self compensating at the aeon’s end.
body: Jung’s last warning (J): the rumour as a living myth whose round form portrays the self, suited “to compensate the splitmindedness of our age.” The Turn reading carries the full compensation row.

passages.text: one thing is certain: they have become a living myth
They are impressive manifestations of totality whose simple, round form portrays the archetype of the self

events.name: Aquarius from the earlier reference star
events.yearDisplay: 1997 CE · conditional calculation in Jung’s footnote
events.oneLine: Jung reports 1997 as one conditional calculation of an Aquarian beginning.
body: Jung gives 1997 when the calculation starts from star “a 113.” He calls the constellation boundary indefinite; this is an alternative calculation in a footnote, not a forecast endorsed by the atlas.

passages.text: Starting from star "O" and assuming a Platonic month of 2,143 years, one would arrive at A.D. 2154 for the beginning of the Aquarian Age, and at A.D. 1997 if you start from star "a 113."

Since the delimitation of the constellations is known to be somewhat arbitrary, this date is very indefinite. It refers to the actual constellation of fixed stars, not to fhe zodion noeton, i.e., the zodiac divided into sectors of 30° each. Astrologically the beginning of the next aeon, according to the starting-point you select, falls between A.D. 2000 and 2200.

events.name: Aquarius from the later reference star
events.yearDisplay: 2154 CE · conditional calculation in Jung’s footnote
events.oneLine: Jung also reports 2154 from another starting star and a 2,143-year month.
body: Jung gives 2154 when the calculation starts from star “O” with a 2,143-year Platonic month. It differs from the earlier alternative and remains qualified. Both markers sit inside the atlas’s broad transition range.

passages.text: Starting from star "O" and assuming a Platonic month of 2,143 years, one would arrive at A.D. 2154 for the beginning of the Aquarian Age, and at A.D. 1997 if you start from star "a 113."

Since the delimitation of the constellations is known to be somewhat arbitrary, this date is very indefinite. It refers to the actual constellation of fixed stars, not to fhe zodion noeton, i.e., the zodiac divided into sectors of 30° each. Astrologically the beginning of the next aeon, according to the starting-point you select, falls between A.D. 2000 and 2200.

threads.name: Christ and Antichrist
threads.oneLine: Jung follows the excluded shadow and the demand to bring opposites into relation.

threads.name: The changing fish
threads.oneLine: Jung compares fish symbols across eras; the line does not assert direct transmission.

threads.name: The alchemical countercurrent
threads.oneLine: Jung follows alchemy’s work on nature, the self, and the union of opposites.

threads.name: The living spirit
threads.oneLine: Jung reads the spirit as an ambivalent mediator rather than a fixed doctrine.

epochs.name: The forecasting years
epochs.oneLine: Every dated Jung forecast of the coming age, 1929 → 1958.
body: The inventory (J): from the 1929 seminar aside to the 1958 Flying Saucers preface — the forecasts gathered, each dated to where Jung spoke it. He forecasts a problem (the union of opposites, the reality of evil), never dated events or a new age-symbol.
Label law: J rows are Jung’s own text; where standard scholarship corrects the astronomy it is marked S and kept beside the claim, never reconciled into it.

passages.text: The spring point is about to enter Aquarius.

epochs.name: The reckoned threshold
epochs.oneLine: The sky-reckonings: 1997, 2154, the third millennium — none of them an event.
body: Every date here is a sky-reckoning and Jung marks the arbitrariness himself: his own two reckonings disagree (1997 vs 2154), the Talmudic world-week runs to A.D. 3239, and fn84 calls the dating “very indefinite.” He dated the sky, not the event, and declined to predict the new age’s content.

S-correction, kept beside the claim: modern constants enter the corpus only as Jung’s citation; the IAU’s 1930 constellation boundaries (not in the corpus) put the ecliptic’s exit from Pisces near A.D. 2600 — later than every date Jung prints.

passages.text: Starting from star "O" and assuming a Platonic month of 2,143 years, one would arrive at A.D. 2154 for the beginning of the Aquarian Age, and at A.D. 1997 if you start from star "a 113."
The constant for the precession is 50.3708 seconds and the total cycle (360°) takes 25,725.6 years

events.name: 29° of Pisces
events.oneLine: The first dated forecast: the spring point “about to enter Aquarius.”
body: Delivered as an aside in the astrology-as-projection frame (J).

passages.text: The spring point is about to enter Aquarius.

events.name: The theosophists’ new age
events.oneLine: Others’ expectation reported: Aquarius as the third condition.
body: Delivered as report (J): the theosophical reading of the coming age in the Joachim frame — Jung citing, not endorsing.

passages.text: people think that the coming of the new age—Aquarius—will be the third condition, the new revelation of the Trinity.

events.name: The time-quality doctrine
events.oneLine: The warrant for any forecast: the moment’s quality stamps what is born in it.
body: Doctrine, not forecast (J): “our own hypothetical time qualities” — the synchronistic bridge on which the whole horizon rests.

passages.text: whatever is born or done at this particular moment of time has the quality of this moment of time.

events.name: The first stars of Aquarius
events.oneLine: “In about 1940 we shall be approaching the first stars of the next sign.”
body: The astronomical-constellation reading (J), with “of course there are no definite lines in the sky” a breath away.

passages.text: In about 1940 we shall be approaching the first stars of the next sign, Aquarius.

events.name: The water-bearer’s ideal
events.oneLine: The sign whose ideal is “the union, the oneness, of animal and divine.”
body: Sky-lore anticipation (J): the iconography read forward — Piscis Austrinus as the Fishes sunk into the unconscious.

passages.text: Aquarius, then, is the sign of the man whose ideal is the union, the oneness, of animal and divine, and in the square the two things are brought together.

events.name: The aerial sign
events.oneLine: Aquarius as air: “the sign of this actual time.”
body: The epoch-reading (J): the spring equinox’s transit into Aquarius read coincident with the mass-movements; Uranus as unforeseen events.

passages.text: Aquarius has always been characterized as an aerial sign, and it has to do with the wind of spring which brings the rain clouds; it is the sign of this actual time, which is the rainy season in those countries where the old Babylonian zodiac originated, in Mesopotamia for instance.

events.name: The vessel-man
events.oneLine: “Aquarius, the man with the vessel to catch whatever flows.”
body: The age’s symbolic task (J), with the powers of darkness “coming up” beside it.

passages.text: The symbol of our time and the coming time is Aquarius, the man with the vessel to catch whatever flows, and he must transform it into the fertile water of life.

events.name: The kairos named Wotan
events.oneLine: The transition read as possession, not progress.
body: The transition-as-possession row (J) — the dark tinge the horizon keeps throughout.

passages.text: it is rather the fault of kairos— the present moment in time—whose name on closer investigation turns out to be Wotan.

events.name: The anti-Christian age
events.oneLine: “Around 125 b.c., the age of Pisces began” — our era its second fish.
body: Position-finding (J): where in the Platonic month we stand, dated to the seminar year.

passages.text: Around 125 b.c., the age of Pisces began, coinciding with the beginnings of Christianity.

events.name: On the threshold
events.oneLine: “Now we are on the threshold of the sign of Aquarius” — the air-age task.
body: The full four-age scheme (J), delivered at the war’s onset: “the spirit is meant to become something subtle again, and man to become who he is” — his boldest content-statement, seminar register.

passages.text: And now we are on the threshold of the sign of Aquarius.
Here the spirit is meant to become something subtle again, and man to become who he is.

events.name: The reckoned dates
events.oneLine: The third millennium; 2154 or 1997 by the starting star — “very indefinite.”
body: The reckoned dates (J), with the arbitrariness conceded in his own footnote: two disagreeing reckonings, fn84’s 2000–2200 range, and the IAU’s later crossing (S, not in corpus) kept beside them.

passages.text: Since then the spring-point has moved along the southern edge of the second fish, and will enter Aquarius in the 82 A clear reference to astrology can be found in Pistis Sophia, where Jesus converses with the "ordainers of the nativity": "But Jesus answered and said to Mary: If the ordainers of the nativity find Heimarmene and the Sphere turned to the left in accordance with their first circulation, then their words will be true, and they will say what must come to pass. But if they find Heimarmene or the Sphere turned to the right, then they will not say anything true, because I have changed their influences and their squares and their triangles and their octants." (Cf. Mead trans., p. 29.) SSThe meridian of the star "0" in the commissure passed through the springpoint in A.D. 11, and that of the star "a 113" in 146 B.C. Calculated on the basis of Peters and Knobel, Ptolemy's Catalogue of Stars. AION course of the third millennium.
Starting from star "O" and assuming a Platonic month of 2,143 years, one would arrive at A.D. 2154 for the beginning of the Aquarian Age, and at A.D. 1997 if you start from star "a 113."

events.name: The union of opposites
events.oneLine: What the new month will constellate: the problem of the union of opposites.
body: THE forecast (J): evil’s real existence to be recognized, the problem solvable “neither by philosophy, nor by economics, nor by politics, but only by the individual human being” — a problem forecast, never a dated event or a new symbol.

passages.text: the approach of the next Platonic month, namely Aquarius, will constellate the problem of the union of opposites.

events.name: The Water Carrier named
events.oneLine: The Talmudic world-week and “the next aeon, that of the Water Carrier.”
body: The chronology row (J): anno mundi 7000 = A.D. 3239, the latest date in the corpus — a pre-modern chronology reported sympathetically, not endorsed as astronomy (S).

passages.text: spring-point will have moved from its present position 18 degrees into Aquarius, the next aeon, that of the Water Carrier.

events.name: Lucifer’s harsh forces
events.oneLine: “Aquarius sets aflame Lucifer’s harsh forces” — the dark-forecast verse.
body: The dark end of the horizon (J): the alchemical emblem deployed against any millenarian optimism — the aeon’s “dark end which we have still to experience.”

passages.text: Luciferi vires accendit Aquarius acres —“Aquarius sets aflame Lucifer’s harsh forces.” Could anyone in his right senses deny that John correctly foresaw at least some of the possible dangers which threaten our world in the final phase of the Christian aeon?

events.name: Pegasus the paranatellon
events.oneLine: The white horse of Revelation as Aquarius’s rising constellation — “may be implied.”
body: Hedged conjecture (J), kept at its own strength: “astrological speculations … may be implied.”

passages.text: Here again astrological speculations concerning the second half of the Christian aeon may be implied, with Pegasus as paranatellon of Aquarius.

events.name: Apocalyptic images
events.oneLine: The horizon as mass-psychological fact: apocalyptic images near the millennium’s end.
body: The kairos row beside it (J): the metamorphosis of the gods, and Coming generations’ account to give.

passages.text: Today, as the end of the second millennium draws near, we are again living in an age filled with apocalyptic images of universal destruction.
Coming generations will have to take account of this momentous transformation

events.name: The footnotes’ checkpoints
events.oneLine: Jung footnoting his own essay against the news: Suez as the shadow’s answer.
body: The empiric checkpoints (J): the essay’s footnotes correcting it against events — the apparatus of a man refusing prophecy’s certainty.

passages.text: the shadow has followed up this overbright picture hotfoot with the Charge of the Light Brigade to Suez.

events.name: Coming events of an era’s end
events.oneLine: The fullest forecast: “coming events which are in accord with the end of an era.”
body: The 1958 preface (J), with the Taurus→Aries→Pisces→Aquarius chain in the same breath — and the ufo-mandala as the change’s sky-symbol.

passages.text: It is not presumption that drives me, but my conscience as a psychiatrist that bids me fulfil my duty and prepare those few who will hear me for coming events which are in accord with the end of an era.

events.name: The dread ticking of the clock
events.oneLine: The transition felt as time-anxiety: the aeons’ rhythm exchanged for the clock.
body: The horizon’s phenomenology (J): what the end of an era does to the people living it.

passages.text: forcing them to exchange the life-preserving rhythm of the aeons for the dread ticking of the clock.

threads.name: The forecast arc
threads.oneLine: 1929 → 1958: every dated forecast, in order — the problem named, the event refused.

epochs.name: Forecast · the cracked dam
epochs.oneLine: Jung forecasts the eruption from the unconscious of his German patients.
body: The arc’s first phase runs from the pre-war baseline to the last seminar years before the seizure of power (J, each row dated). The 1914 row is retrospective — written in 1936 — and the 1918 forecast rests on the printed essay, not on surviving case records.
“Wotan” as the name of the eruption is Jung’s heretical suggestion, offered as his claim about history, not as established history (S keeps the historians’ economic and political factors).

passages.text: As the Christian view of the world loses its authority, the more menacingly will the “blond beast” be heard prowling about in its underground prison, ready at any moment to burst out with devastating consequences.

epochs.name: Eruption · the possession
epochs.oneLine: Wotan’s fires: a nation reviving an archaic symbol at mass scale.
body: The essays and seminars of 1933–38 name what Jung watched: the counter-sun, the possession, the kairos whose name turns out to be Wotan (J). His own risk-flag stands with the claim: he calls the suggestion heretical and labels it his mantic reading.

passages.text: In fact I venture the heretical suggestion that the unfathomable depths of Wotan’s character explain more of National Socialism than all three reasonable factors put together.

epochs.name: Catastrophe · the epidemic
epochs.oneLine: “The first outbreak of epidemic insanity”: the myth fulfilled in ruins.
body: The post-mortem rows (J): the epidemic-insanity diagnosis, the personified shadow, the projection-return law — Jung reading the catastrophe his forecast had named.

passages.text: The phenomenon we have witnessed in Germany was nothing less than the first outbreak of epidemic insanity, an irruption of the unconscious into what seemed to be a tolerably well-ordered world.

epochs.name: Compensation · the counter-move
epochs.oneLine: What surfaces against the eruption: the Assumption, the ufo-mandala, the kairos.
body: The compensation rows (J): the 1950 Assumption as the feminine counter-move, the sky-mandala of the saucer rumour as the self’s symbol at the turn, the kairos for a “metamorphosis of the gods.” Not all compensations are light — the seminar years’ dark counter-saviors stand in the forecast phase.

passages.text: They are impressive manifestations of totality whose simple, round form portrays the archetype of the self

epochs.name: Horizon · Aquarius
epochs.oneLine: The turn’s forward edge: the threshold of the sign of Aquarius.
body: The arc ends looking forward (J): the 1940 element-scheme’s air-age, the 1958 warning of “coming events which are in accord with the end of an era.” What Jung forecast for the coming age is gathered in the Aquarius Horizon reading; he dates the sky, never the event.
The horizon boundary 2154 is one of Jung’s own two conditional reckonings (fn84), kept as a display edge, not a prediction (S notes the IAU’s constellation boundaries put the crossing far later).

passages.text: We are living in what the Greeks called the καιρός— the right moment—for a “metamorphosis of the gods,” of the fundamental principles and symbols.

events.name: The world before 1914
events.oneLine: The rationalist world-order as the cracked dam — seen from 1936.
body: Retrospective baseline (J): the “Wotan” essay opens on the inconceivability of the pre-war world and the witches’ sabbath that followed.

passages.text: When we look back to the time before 1914, we find ourselves living in a world of events which would have been inconceivable before the war.
And what came after the war was a veritable witches’ sabbath.

events.name: The blond beast forecast
events.oneLine: “The ‘blond beast’ … prowling about in its underground prison.”
body: The 1918 essay’s forecast (J), re-read aloud by Jung in 1934 as “a rather good diagnosis of the present political conditions.” The clinical prehistory he later claimed (¶447, written 1946) rests on self-report; the printed forecast is the checkable witness.

passages.text: As the Christian view of the world loses its authority, the more menacingly will the “blond beast” be heard prowling about in its underground prison, ready at any moment to burst out with devastating consequences.

events.name: “Discover our shadow”
events.oneLine: The war named as the shadow’s price, two years before the seizure of power.
body: Seminar aside (J): without the shadow-work, “we are driven into a world war in order to see what beasts we are.”

passages.text: We have to discover our shadow.

events.name: The oak and the Goddess of Reason
events.oneLine: Wotan’s oak hewn, Reason enthroned: two depositions, no thunderbolt.
body: The deposal pairing (J): 1793’s Goddess of Reason and the missionaries’ hewing of Wotan’s oak — both gods felled with no avenging bolt, both with the god’s return in store.

passages.text: The enthronement of the Goddess of Reason in Notre Dame seems to have been a symbolic gesture of great significance for the Western world—rather like the hewing down of Wotan’s oak by Christian missionaries. On both occasions no avenging bolt from heaven struck the blasphemer down.

events.name: Wotan’s fires
events.oneLine: “Those swastika people are building Wotan’s fires again” — five years early.
body: The naming before the essay (J): the 1931 seminar aside that the 1936 “Wotan” paper later argued at length.

passages.text: And in Germany those National Socialists, those swastika people, are building Wotan's fires again.

events.name: The iron wolf’s child
events.oneLine: A white placenta, a child suckled by an iron wolf: the dark counter-savior born.
body: The seminar vision-row’s darkest birth (J): “the birth of a most dangerous warlike spirit, fed by a wolf with iron milk” — the age’s war-charge in symbol, three years before the counter-sun reading and the essay.

passages.text: From a white placenta emerged a creature in the shape of a child.
Whilst our patient's unconscious points to the birth of a most dangerous warlike spirit, fed by a wolf with iron milk.

events.name: The forecast re-read
events.oneLine: Jung reads his 1918 article aloud: “a rather good diagnosis.”
body: Self-verification in public (J): one of the few forecasts Jung re-confirmed against his own earlier print while the events ran.

passages.text: I published an article which I will translate to you, as it is a rather good diagnosis of the present political conditions.

events.name: The counter-sun
events.oneLine: The swastika turning the wrong way: black, left-turning, a counter-sun.
body: The seminar reading (J): the arrested progress of a sun-wheel turned backwards — the symbol read live as the eruption ran.

passages.text: And those rather competent National Socialists to whom I talked in Germany did not know that their swastika was turning the wrong way.

events.name: A nation revives an archaic symbol
events.oneLine: The Wotan eruption generalized: mass emotion revolutionizing individual life.
body: The 1936 generalization (J): the archaic symbol luring “millions of warriors ready for death” — “all this absurdity is a horrible reality.”

passages.text: Can we not see how a whole nation is reviving an archaic symbol, yes, even archaic religious forms, and how this mass emotion is influencing and revolutionizing the life of the individual in a catastrophic manner? The man of the past is alive in us today to a degree undreamt of before the war, and in the last analysis what is the fate of great nations but a summation of the psychic changes in individuals?

events.name: The churches seized
events.oneLine: German Christians, and Valhalla preached from a funeral pulpit.
body: The footnote record (J): the Protestant movement inside the church, and Langmann in S.A. uniform directing the Gustloff dead “to Valhalla.”

passages.text: A National Socialist movement inside the Protestant Church, which tried to eliminate all vestiges of the Old Testament from Christianity.
Langmann, an evangelical clergyman and high dignitary of the Church, at the funeral of the late Gustloff.

events.name: “The longexpected Antichrist”
events.oneLine: “Our blight is ideologies—they are the longexpected Antichrist!”
body: The aeon-name applied to politics (J): the Antichrist doctrine landing on the mass-movements of the age.

passages.text: Our blight is ideologies—they are the longexpected Antichrist!

events.name: The parallel symptom-track
events.oneLine: “Just as Christianity had a cross … so Hitler has a swastika.”
body: The symptom comparison (J), with the War of the Worlds panic beside it as the latent-emotion precedent.

passages.text: Just as Christianity had a cross to symbolize its essential teaching, so Hitler has a swastika, a symbol as old and widespread as the cross.

events.name: “Wotan”: the essay
events.oneLine: The heretical suggestion: kairos whose name, on closer investigation, is Wotan.
body: THE ESSAY (J): Nostradamus motto, the white-horse sect, Ergriffenheit, the kairos naming, and the mantic close — “National Socialism would not be the last word.” Jung labels the core claim heresy himself; the vault keeps it as his claim, not history (S).

passages.text: In fact I venture the heretical suggestion that the unfathomable depths of Wotan’s character explain more of National Socialism than all three reasonable factors put together.
it is rather the fault of kairos— the present moment in time—whose name on closer investigation turns out to be Wotan.
If this conclusion is correct, National Socialism would not be the last word.

events.name: “The beginning of the holocaust”
events.oneLine: The dated aside: “we are now exactly in the beginning of the holocaust.”
body: Preserved verbatim (J), no more weight claimed: the sacrificial-conflagration sense in seminar speech, three years before the war — the word’s later history is not Jung’s meaning here.

passages.text: I rather insist upon these passages, because we are now exactly in the beginning of the holocaust.

events.name: The aeon scheme in a child’s dream
events.oneLine: Taurus → Aries → Pisces → “the threshold of the sign of Aquarius.”
body: The full element-cycle taught at the war’s onset (J): air assigned to Aquarius — “the spirit is meant to become something subtle again, and man to become who he is.”

passages.text: And now we are on the threshold of the sign of Aquarius.
Here the spirit is meant to become something subtle again, and man to become who he is.

events.name: The dark brother
events.oneLine: “My unexpectedly dark brother … though I deny it a thousand times, it is also in me.”
body: The shadow internalized (J): the European’s own antichristian Neo-Paganism, owned rather than projected.

passages.text: As a European, I am burdened most heavily by my unexpectedly dark brother, who confronts me with his antichristian Neo-Paganism.
And though I deny it a thousand times, it is also in me.

events.name: Possession at war’s height
events.oneLine: “European man was possessed by something that robbed him of all free will.”
body: The possession doctrine written mid-war (J): unconscious possession ending only with the scare of our “god-almightiness” — and only individuals, “for the masses are blind brutes.”

passages.text: Nobody realized that European man was possessed by something that robbed him of all free will.

And this state of unconscious possession will continue undeterred until we Europeans become scared of our “god-almightiness.” Such a change can begin only with individuals, for the masses are blind brutes, as we know to our cost.

events.name: After the catastrophe
events.oneLine: Epidemic insanity, the personified shadow, the mass psychoses named.
body: The post-mortem rows (J): “He represented the shadow, the inferior part of everybody’s personality”; “the political mass movements of our time are psychic epidemics.” Jung’s own ethnic psychology of the 1918/1934 stratum stands in the vault as his claim, historically compromised — not softened here.

passages.text: He represented the shadow, the inferior part of everybody’s personality, in an overwhelming degree, and this was another reason why they fell for him.
the political mass movements of our time are psychic epidemics, in other words, mass psychoses.

events.name: The Assumption
events.oneLine: The dogma as compensating symptom in an age of the greatest political schism.
body: The feminine counter-move (J): the hydrogen-bomb age arming itself “for a stupendous crime,” and against it the Mother of God enthroned — for Jung the most important religious event since the Reformation, foretelling the god-image’s incarnation in creaturely man.

passages.text: Humanity is arming itself, in dread and fascinated horror, for a stupendous crime.

The dogma of the Assumption, proclaimed in an age suffering from the greatest political schism history has ever known, is a compensating symptom that reflects the strivings of science for a uniform world-picture.
I consider to be the most important religious event since the Reformation.

events.name: The kairos of the gods’ metamorphosis
events.oneLine: “We are living in what the Greeks called the kairos — the right moment.”
body: The last framing (J): the moment for a “metamorphosis of the gods,” with the H-bomb question standing beside it.

passages.text: We are living in what the Greeks called the καιρός— the right moment—for a “metamorphosis of the gods,” of the fundamental principles and symbols.
Coming generations will have to take account of this momentous transformation

events.name: The ufo-mandala
events.oneLine: A living myth of round totalities: “remember his own soul … wholeness.”
body: The compensation in the sky (J), opened as a self-declared second Wotan warning. Jung’s own risk-flag stays with it: the reflection comes “perilously close to those turbid fantasies which becloud the minds of world-reformers” — “But I must take this risk” (¶590).

passages.text: It is not presumption that drives me, but my conscience as a psychiatrist that bids me fulfil my duty and prepare those few who will hear me for coming events which are in accord with the end of an era.
one thing is certain: they have become a living myth
They bid each of us remember his own soul and his own wholeness, because this is the answer the West should give to the danger of mass-mindedness.

events.name: “Wotan’s host” still roams
events.oneLine: The wizard with the Merseburg spell-book: the god’s “timelessness.”
body: The bridge row (J): the eruption’s god not a closed chapter but a standing presence in the Swiss cantons — the arc handed to the horizon.

passages.text: Anyone who does not know that “Wotan’s host”—enlightenment or no enlightenment—still roams about our Swiss cantons

threads.name: The Wotan arc
threads.oneLine: From the deposed oak to Wotan’s host still roaming: the eruption row.

threads.name: The counter-sun
threads.oneLine: The swastika rows: the age’s symbol turned backwards.

threads.name: The dark counter-saviors
threads.oneLine: Not all compensations are round and light: the shadow owned.

threads.name: The compensation
threads.oneLine: What surfaces against the eruption: the scheme, the Assumption, the sky-mandala.
